# netactuate_router_vrf_ipsec_peer (Resource)

Beta. The cloud router family is in beta: behaviour and schema may change. Manages an IPsec peer in a cloud router VRF.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netactuate_router_vrf_ipsec_peer" "example" {
  name         = "example"
  psk_secret   = "change-me-example-value"
  remote_id    = "example"
  router_id    = 12345
  vrf_id       = 12345
  overlay_ipv4 = "192.0.2.1/30"
  peer_address = "192.0.2.2"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the IPSec peer.
- `psk_secret` (String, Sensitive) Pre-shared key (1-256 chars).
- `remote_id` (String) Remote peer identifier (1-64 chars).
- `router_id` (Number) The ID of the cloud router.
- `vrf_id` (Number) The ID of the VRF.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the IPSec peer.
- `do_initiate_connection` (Boolean) Whether to initiate or respond to connection.
- `overlay_ipv4` (String) Overlay tunnel IPv4 CIDR.
- `overlay_ipv6` (String) Overlay tunnel IPv6 CIDR.
- `peer_address` (String) Remote router IPv4 address. Required when do_initiate_connection is true. Cannot be set in passive mode (do_initiate_connection = false).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ipsec_peer_id` (Number) The IPSec peer ID.
- `local_id` (String) Local router ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import netactuate_router_vrf_ipsec_peer.example 12345
```
